short: Standard sensor (M05) and decoder (M06): one throat strain channel, small CNN. 95.25% on 20 words, with split grouping and production mode unstated, does not show silent, session-independent decoding.
position: The paper changes the sensor (M05), a single graphene-textile strain channel in a throat choker, and the decoder (M06), a compact 1D CNN with recorded-noise augmentation; both are standard, since the same group had already decoded words from a single graphene strain gauge on the throat and CNNs are common closed-vocabulary classifiers. The claim that sensor sensitivity is what lets one channel and a small network reach 95.25% is untested: no lower-sensitivity sensor, channel or augmentation ablation is run on the same words. The evaluation (M12) leaves the split grouping unstated, pools three participants and reports no chance level or repeated runs, so the accuracies do not show session- or speaker-independent decoding. The paper never states whether the words were mouthed or voiced (M04).
